subject: A metal sheet bolted into a frame, cut away in isometric with its mesh lines bent into the standing wave, a striker rod over one point, a stylus at another and a felt damper hanging above the edge.
controls: size: count and scale, the mesh goes from 4 to 12 lines a side and the plate and frame grow about 1.5x in footprint.
tension: shape, the sheet's surface (mesh polylines) goes from a slack single dome to a taut, finer, inharmonic ripple.
damp: position, the felt damper drops from 40 px above the plate at 0 onto its dashed footprint at 100.
pickup: position, the stylus pin slides across the sheet from beside the striker to the far corner.
reference: library/theseus-tower (line drawing, black bodies with grey outlines, one projection)
risks: The bent mesh is a 3D surface: with 12 x 12 lines it needs mutable outlines well past the 4-path limit, so surface shape must come from pre-drawn variants or translated segments; tension may have to collapse to a few stepped surfaces. The striker head and damper are small (10 px) and could read as icons at 1:1. Grid lines at size 12 come within ~9 px, fine, but hidden-line over self-occluding ripples isn't modelled yet.
